industry.headline: UK moves toward spring 2027 under-16 social media ban with parliamentary regulations expected by year-end
industry.summary: The UK confirmed it will lay regulations by year-end for a spring 2027 under-16 social media ban, extending beyond Australia's model to block livestreaming and stranger contact, with default overnight curfews (midnight-6am) for 16-17 year-olds already in force since July 2026. This directly validates NOMO's value proposition in the UK pilot market where CEO Leonardo is already engaged in policy discussions.

industry.headline: Adolescent Social Media Addiction MDL grows to 3,208 pending actions
industry.summary: The MDL against major platforms now covers 3,208 pending actions, including a first school-district bellwether settlement (Breathitt County School District). Scale of district-level litigation signals K-12 institutions actively seeking remedies for social-media harm — a tailwind for NOMO's rewards-based school pitch as an alternative to pure restriction/litigation.

industry.headline: Meta reaches $17.1B settlement with 51 state attorneys general over teen addiction claims
industry.summary: Meta agreed to pay up to $17.1B to settle claims it designed Instagram/Facebook to be addictive for teens, with the deal requiring daily time limits and overnight restrictions pending court approval. This landmark enforcement action validates the core compulsive-screen-time problem NOMO addresses and sets a policy template likely to increase demand for third-party reward-based alternatives like NOMO.

industry.headline: Brazil's ECA Digital child-safety law implementation continues, with congressional debate on extending to a full under-16 access ban
industry.summary: Brazilian lawmakers are debating extending the existing ECA Digital age-verification framework toward an outright under-16 social media ban, building on Brazil's school phone-restriction law credited with improved learning and engagement. As NOMO's first and most established market (São Paulo/Rio contracts), continued regulatory tightening strengthens institutional demand for NOMO's model.
